plain_text:
1 | P a g e 
City of Concord
Trustees of Trust Fund Meeting
Minutes of October 21st, 2026 Meeting
Meeting was convened at 8:40 AM at City Hall, 41 Green Street, Concord.
In attendance: Trustee Susan Dunton, Trustee Sabrina Beavens, Trustee Travis Craig, Corey Boucher of 
Citizens Bank Wealth Management Group, Laurie Leduc of Citizens Bank (virtually); Chelsey Michalski and 
Sarah Gerlack from the City of Concord
Minutes from the July 16, 2026 and September 29,2026 meeting were distributed for review, no comments or 
discussion. All in favor, minutes approved.
Presentation by Corey Boucher:
 As we head into the Halloween season, the third quarter saw parallels to a recurring horror movie
villain. Inflation, which was thought to have been conquered, returned in the second quarter and 
caused economic markets to stumble. Increased oil, gas, and especially diesel prices have put 
steady upward pressure on overall economic inflation, causing the downward trend of 2025 to 
reverse back upward. 
 The inflation rate stands at 3.4%, which the Federal Reserve feels is too high and does not like 
the fact that inflation has stalled in the mid 3% instead of continuing the trend down to 2% 
annualized inflation. This meant that the Federal Reserve chose to raise interest rates by 0.25% 
in September and has hinted that there may need to be another rate hike towards the end of the 
year. 
 Equity markets have taken the rate hike in the stride. Buoyed by strong earning and continued AI
investment, US stocks were generally higher, but results were mixed depending on the sector and
company. Throughout the quarter, the Iran War shifted to reduced standoff with continued, but 
limited violence.  Oil tankers are able to make it through the Strait of Hormuz to some extent, 
and estimates are that about 75% of prewar shipment volume are getting through today (but it 
cost shippers much more).
 Business spending remains healthy and the consumer reports sentiment that is downbeat, but 
retail spending continues to grow. 
 Year to date, the total portfolio is now up by 4.5%, net of fees, after having a Q3 where the 
portfolio dipped 0.1%. Despite this slight drop, the portfolio’s bias toward short term fixed 
income and quality fixed income meant that fixed income outperformed the bond market. Large 
cap equity, the next biggest allocation, also outperformed the S&P 500 benchmark slightly.
 Fixed income returns have turned negative for the year, being down nearly 2.5%. Higher 
inflation and structural debt issues, combined with a federal reserve that has demonstrated it can 
raise interest rates if needed, have pushed bond yields higher and depressed bond values. 
Forward yields look pretty good, however, with 10-year treasury bond yielding 5.22%
 Looking ahead, the midterm elections are the next big event on the calendar. We continue to 
favor equity on the back of strong company earnings, but will reduce the equity overweight 
slightly to shift to some fixed income at these attractive yields.
 The Concord Trust Funds performance surpassed Q3 benchmarks despite posting slightly down 
returns on and absolute basis. 
Trustee Travis Craig had questions concerning investing with technology companies and how Artificial 
Intelligence would affect those companies’ ratings.  Corey explained that there is still a lot of growth 
with AI and that there would be no immediate affect with continuing to invest with those companies.
Trustee Sabrina Beavens had concerns with investing in Palantir Technologies Inc with their 
involvement in various government contracts. Discussion ensued between Corey from Citizens Bank 
and the Trustees. It was agreed that if Trustees wanted to put to any specific companies on the “Do Not 
Buy List”, it could be discussed and voted on. The Trustees will revisit this concern at the next quarterly
meeting. 
The next quarterly meeting date was set for January 21, 2027 at 8:30am at Concord City Hall.
Meeting adjourned at 9:21am.
Respectfully Submitted,
Sarah Gerlack – Deputy Treasurer
